title: A procurable on-premise occupier removes the sovereignty wedge entirely
content:
Flowable AG is headquartered in Zurich with an office in Berlin, offers first-party *"Cloud-based"*, *"On-premise"* and *"Hybrid"* deployment, holds SOC 2, ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance, and names government among its verticals.

The screening rule this corpus uses is that where a vendor has filled the gap, the only remaining opening is that the occupying solution cannot be procured under EU or German public-sector rules. A Swiss vendor with a German office selling an on-premise deployment under ISO 27001 does not create that opening.

What remains is a commercial objection — Enterprise costs money — which means competing on price and features against an incumbent with 600-plus enterprise customers in its own category. That is a different and much harder proposition than filling an empty slot, and it is the basis for the DEAD END verdict.
description: Flowable Enterprise is sold on-premise by a Swiss vendor with a German office under ISO 27001 and GDPR, so no EU procurement exclusion remains to argue from.
